Triggered auto assignment to Contributor-plus team member for initial proposal review - @samranahm (`External`)

🤖 Web test steps verification results: ⚠️ partial Created a disposable $1.07 expense and comment. Verification stopped at an unsupported right-click operation, so the reported navigation bug remains unverified. | Step | Status | |------|--------| |
Open Spend > ExpensesInitially empty; the disposable expense appeared after creation.

| ✅ | |

| ❌ | |
Click the parent commentBlocked before entering the thread.
| ❌ | |
Click expense header Back → Spend > ExpensesNot executed from the required thread-origin state.
| ❌ | ### Preliminary analysis — low confidence **Suspected mechanism:** Parent-comment navigation can open another expense panel above the thread. Its Back button then pops that panel, revealing the thread instead of Spend.
Code evidence and important counterevidence - The parent-comment click invokes the linked-report navigation helper: [AncestorReportActionItem.tsx:121–142](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d7c37c01c1f789576fce663d34cc8255e4a55f51/src/pages/inbox/report/AncestorReportActionItem.tsx#L121-L142). - Its fallback opens the ancestor expense with `backTo: SearchReport`: [ReportUtils.ts:12454–12461](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d7c37c01c1f789576fce663d34cc8255e4a55f51/src/libs/ReportUtils.ts#L12454-L12461). - The header interprets that value as ordinary history-back, consistent with returning to the thread: [ReportHeader.tsx:60–82](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d7c37c01c1f789576fce663d34cc8255e4a55f51/src/pages/inbox/ReportHeader.tsx#L60-L82). **However**, the helper already checks whether the original expense is immediately below the thread. If found, it updates that expense and pops the thread rather than opening another panel: [ReportUtils.ts:12440–12452](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d7c37c01c1f789576fce663d34cc8255e4a55f51/src/libs/ReportUtils.ts#L12440-L12452). That should prevent the reported behavior in the straightforward stack. The unresolved question is **why this protection misses in the affected flow**. A different stack shape or deployed implementation remains possible. The QA-linked [unsafe-assertion refactor](https://github.com/Expensify/App/pull/104926) does not establish causation: its relevant header changes are type-only, and the Back behavior [already existed before that merge](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ea4ecf7b01ad2dcc34453f5d80457ef7a7386640/src/pages/inbox/ReportHeader.tsx#L51-L73).
**Required before recommending a fix:** Capture the active panel stack, ancestor report ID, and selected navigation branch immediately before and after clicking the parent comment. This will distinguish a missed existing-expense match from a different navigation failure. Add regression coverage for the complete sequence through the final Back action; reverting type annotations is not supported by the evidence. --- _[view run](https://github.com/Expensify/melvin/actions/runs/45331848439)_ · _[view recording](https://melvinbot-assets.exops.io/session-45331848439-1-d30a5824-503c-4b5b-8a6b-136b894120e7.webm)_

## Proposal

Reproduced on staging web. The route IDs show the cause directly:
1. Spend > Expenses → expense: `/search/view/6668534542846014?anchorTransactionID=...` (the **expense report**).
2. Comment → Reply in thread: `/search/view/5808396084513355` (the thread).
3. Click the parent comment: a **new** screen `/search/view/8951406895024852/<reportActionID>?backTo=SearchReport` is pushed. `8951406895024852` is the expense's **one-transaction thread**, not the expense report below.
4. `<` → back on the thread (`5808396084513355`) instead of Spend > Expenses.

### What is the root cause of that problem?

When the user clicks the parent comment, `AncestorReportActionItem` calls `navigateToLinkedReportAction`. In the RHP it already has a guard for this exact flow: if the route under the thread is the ancestor's report, it updates that route and pops the thread instead of pushing a new screen:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/main/src/libs/ReportUtils.ts#L12440-L12452

The guard misses because of **one-expense reports**. Opening an expense from Spend > Expenses opens `SEARCH_REPORT` with the **expense report's** ID (`/search/view/<expenseReportID>?anchorTransactionID=...`). In that combined view, comments are posted to the **one-transaction thread**, not the expense report (`useComposerReportData` → `getOneTransactionThreadReportID`). So:

- `ancestor.report.reportID` is the transaction thread ID.
- `routeBelow.params.reportID` is the expense report ID, which is the transaction thread's parent.

They never match. The code falls through to `Navigation.navigate(ROUTES.SEARCH_REPORT.getRoute({reportID: <transaction thread>, ...}))` and pushes a third screen on top of the thread. Pressing `<` on that screen pops back to the thread, which is the reported bug.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

In `navigateToLinkedReportAction`, make the existing "route below" guard also recognize the expense report that displays the ancestor transaction thread:

1. Compute `isAncestorShownInRouteBelow`:
   - true if `routeBelowParams.reportID === ancestor.report.reportID` (today's case);
   - or if the ancestor is a transaction thread (`isReportTransactionThread(ancestor.report)`) and `routeBelowParams.reportID === ancestor.report.parentReportID`, i.e. the screen below is the one-expense report that renders that thread's actions.
2. When it's true, keep today's behaviour: `setParams({reportActionID})` on the route below so the combined view scrolls to and highlights the parent comment, then `Navigation.goBack()` to pop the thread.
3. Everything else is unchanged:
   - Multi-expense reports and other ancestors still push `SEARCH_REPORT` as today.
   - The wide-layout (non-RHP) branch is unchanged.

After the fix: thread → click parent comment → back on the expense with the comment highlighted → `<` returns to Spend > Expenses.

**Tests** (unit tests for `navigateToLinkedReportAction` with a mocked RHP state):
- Route below = expense report and ancestor = its one-transaction thread: `setParams` on the route below plus `goBack`, and no `navigate`.
- Route below = same report ID as the ancestor: same as above (existing behaviour preserved).
- Route below is an unrelated report: `navigate(SEARCH_REPORT)` as today.
- Ancestor is a non-transaction-thread report whose `parentReportID` matches the route below: still `navigate` (the new branch only applies to transaction threads).

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

- **Change the `backTo` / back-button handling in `ReportHeader`** so `<` skips the thread. That treats the symptom: the extra screen would still be pushed, and the stack would keep a duplicate expense screen.
- **Navigate with the expense report ID instead of the thread ID in the fallback.** That still pushes a duplicate of the screen already below. Reusing the route below, like the existing guard does, is cleaner.

## Proposal

### What is the root cause of that problem?

The "already open below" guard in `navigateToLinkedReportAction` compares the wrong report IDs when an expense was opened from Spend > Expenses and belongs to a **single-expense report**, so clicking the parent comment pushes a duplicate RHP screen instead of popping back.

1. **Spend opens the expense report, not the transaction thread.** For a single-expense report, the Spend list keeps `reportID = transactionItem.reportID` (the expense **report**) and only switches to `reportAction.childReportID` (the transaction thread) for self-DM or multi-expense reports: [Search/index.tsx#L787-L794](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d7c37c01c1f789576fce663d34cc8255e4a55f51/src/components/Search/index.tsx#L787-L794). It then opens `SEARCH_REPORT` with that expense report ID: [Search/index.tsx#L898-L910](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d7c37c01c1f789576fce663d34cc8255e4a55f51/src/components/Search/index.tsx#L898-L910).
2. **Comments are stored on the transaction thread.** In that combined single-expense view, the composer writes comments to `effectiveTransactionThreadReportID ?? reportID`: [useComposerSubmit.ts#L51-L52](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d7c37c01c1f789576fce663d34cc8255e4a55f51/src/pages/inbox/report/ReportActionCompose/useComposerSubmit.ts#L51-L52) via [useComposerReportData.ts#L32-L35](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d7c37c01c1f789576fce663d34cc8255e4a55f51/src/pages/inbox/report/ReportActionCompose/useComposerReportData.ts#L32-L35). "Reply in thread" therefore creates a child of the **transaction thread** and pushes it as another `SEARCH_REPORT` onto the same RHP ([Report/index.ts#L3055-L3061](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d7c37c01c1f789576fce663d34cc8255e4a55f51/src/libs/actions/Report/index.ts#L3055-L3061)), leaving the RHP stack as `[SEARCH_REPORT(expenseReportID), SEARCH_REPORT(commentThreadID)]`.
3. **The guard misses.** Clicking the parent comment ([AncestorReportActionItem.tsx#L124-L139](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d7c37c01c1f789576fce663d34cc8255e4a55f51/src/pages/inbox/report/AncestorReportActionItem.tsx#L124-L139)) calls `navigateToLinkedReportAction`, whose guard only goes back when `routeBelowParams.reportID === ancestor.report.reportID` ([ReportUtils.ts#L12440-L12452](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d7c37c01c1f789576fce663d34cc8255e4a55f51/src/libs/ReportUtils.ts#L12440-L12452)). Here `ancestor.report` is the **transaction thread**, whereas `routeBelow` holds its parent **expense report**, so the IDs differ and the fallback pushes `SEARCH_REPORT({reportID: transactionThreadID, reportActionID, backTo: SEARCH_REPORT})` ([ReportUtils.ts#L12454-L12461](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d7c37c01c1f789576fce663d34cc8255e4a55f51/src/libs/ReportUtils.ts#L12454-L12461)).
4. **The duplicate screen is not redirected away.** `OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler` deliberately skips routes that include `reportActionID` ([OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler.tsx#L86-L91](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d7c37c01c1f789576fce663d34cc8255e4a55f51/src/pages/inbox/OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler.tsx#L86-L91)), so the pushed transaction-thread screen remains above the comment thread. Its header Back button sees `backTo === SCREENS.RIGHT_MODAL.SEARCH_REPORT` and calls plain `Navigation.goBack()` ([ReportHeader.tsx#L65-L68](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d7c37c01c1f789576fce663d34cc8255e4a55f51/src/pages/inbox/ReportHeader.tsx#L65-L68)), returning to the comment thread instead of Spend > Expenses.

This also explains why the guard already works for multi-expense reports and self-DM expenses: in those flows Spend opens the transaction thread itself, so the IDs match.

### What changes do you think we should make in order to solve the problem?

In `navigateToLinkedReportAction` ([ReportUtils.ts#L12440-L12452](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d7c37c01c1f789576fce663d34cc8255e4a55f51/src/libs/ReportUtils.ts#L12440-L12452)), extend the "ancestor is already open below" check to also recognize the combined single-expense report case:

- Keep the existing exact match (`routeBelowParams.reportID === ancestor.report.reportID`).
- Also treat `routeBelow` as a match when `routeBelowParams.reportID === ancestor.report.parentReportID` **and** `ancestor.report` is specifically that parent's **one-transaction thread**, verified with the existing `isOneTransactionThread(ancestor.report, parentReport, parentReportAction)` helper ([ReportUtils.ts#L3053-L3071](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d7c37c01c1f789576fce663d34cc8255e4a55f51/src/libs/ReportUtils.ts#L3053-L3071)) using the Onyx report and parent report action lookups already in `ReportUtils`. Checking `isOneTransactionThread` rather than only `isReportTransactionThread` is critical so a **multi-expense** parent report sitting below in the RHP (which does not render its child transaction threads' comments inline) does not false-match and pop away from the transaction thread.
- When either condition matches, keep the existing behavior: call `setParams({reportActionID})` on `routeBelow` so the combined single-expense view scrolls to and highlights the parent comment, then call `Navigation.goBack()`. The RHP stack cleanly returns to `[SEARCH_REPORT(expenseReportID)]`, and tapping `<` closes the RHP back to Spend > Expenses.

No changes are needed in `ReportHeader`, `OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler`, or `Search/index.tsx`, preserving multi-expense/self-DM flows, `reportActionID` deep links, and the non-RHP (`isInNarrowPaneModal === false`) path.

Add unit test coverage for `navigateToLinkedReportAction` verifying:
- RHP stack `[SEARCH_REPORT(singleExpenseParentReport), SEARCH_REPORT(commentThread)]` with a one-transaction-thread ancestor calls `setParams` + `goBack` and does not call `navigate`.
- RHP stack where `routeBelow` is a **multi-expense** parent report (not a one-transaction thread) still falls through to `navigate` instead of popping back to the parent report.
- Existing exact-ID match and unrelated-report cases remain unchanged.

### What alternative solutions did you explore? (Optional)

- **Checking only `isReportTransactionThread(ancestor.report)` with `parentReportID`:** Rejected because any transaction thread under a multi-expense report also passes `isReportTransactionThread`, which would falsely pop back to a multi-expense parent report that does not render that transaction's comments inline.
- **Letting `OneTransactionThreadRedirectHandler` redirect even when `reportActionID` is set:** Rejected because the redirected screen would still sit above the comment thread on the RHP stack (so Back would still land on the thread) and it would regress comment deep links into one-transaction threads.
- **Altering `ReportHeader` Back behavior for `backTo === SEARCH_REPORT`:** Rejected because it masks the duplicate screen on the stack and would break legitimate report-to-report back navigation in Search.

@samranahm Melvin's analysis leaves open why the route-below check in `navigateToLinkedReportAction` misses, and the answer is the IDs: for a one-expense report, Spend opens the RHP on the expense report's `reportID`, not the transaction thread's:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d7c37c01c1f789576fce663d34cc8255e4a55f51/src/components/Search/index.tsx#L787-L795

Comments typed in that combined view are written to the transaction thread instead:

https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/d7c37c01c1f789576fce663d34cc8255e4a55f51/src/pages/inbox/report/ReportActionCompose/useComposerSubmit.ts#L51-L52

So in the reply thread `ancestor.report` is the transaction thread, the `reportID` comparison fails, and the fallback pushes a `SEARCH_REPORT` for it with `backTo: SCREENS.RIGHT_MODAL.SEARCH_REPORT`, whose Back pops straight to the thread; I tested this locally — after clicking the parent comment the RHP stack is `[expense report, thread, transaction thread]`, and Back lands on the thread. Treating the route below as a match when it is the one-expense parent of `ancestor.report` (its `parentReportID`) and just popping back to it fixes this inside that one helper, without touching Search or the composer.

Happy to put up a full proposal for this if that's useful.
